title: Inverted scale update formula in concentrated liquidity breaks invariant allowing economic exploitation

title: Critical: non_native_signed_call permits forged signed-origin execution (Chainflip)

title: Transaction deserialization uses attacker-controlled length in Vec::with_capacity (NEAR)

title: Raydium CLMM tick manipulation via unvalidated TickArrayBitmapExtension
summary: Immunefi bounty of $505k in RAY. increase_liquidity() took remaining_accounts[0] as the TickArrayBitmapExtension without checking it belonged to the pool, so an attacker could flip tick statuses in the bitmap and add or remove liquidity at arbitrary price points; fixed by validating the extension account.

title: Yield Protocol strategy burn() over-credits LP tokens after direct donation
summary: Immunefi bounty of $95k USDC. The strategy's burn() sized the LP payout from pool.balanceOf(address(this)) instead of tracked deposits, so an attacker could send extra LP tokens to inflate the balance and withdraw more base tokens than the position was worth.

title: Silo Finance utilization-rate manipulation through donated assets
summary: Immunefi bounty of $100k USDC. Donating assets to a Silo market with zero initial deposits made the attacker the majority shareholder, letting them manipulate the utilization rate and interest calculation to borrow more than the system should allow.

title: DFX Finance EURS rounding error mints pool shares on zero-value transfers
summary: Immunefi bounty of $100k USDT. AssimilatorV2 mishandled EURS (2 decimals): repeated deposits small enough to transfer zero tokens still minted Curve pool shares, letting the attacker progressively take over the pool without providing liquidity; fixed by requiring amount transferred > 0.

title: Enzyme Finance GSN preRelayedCall missing forwarder validation
summary: Immunefi bounty of $400k. preRelayedCall() in the Gas Station Network integration did not validate the forwarder address, so a malicious forwarder could relay calls, manipulate fees and drain funds from the vault.

title: Frontier pallet msg.value truncation (256 to 128 bits) across Moonbeam, Astar and Acala
summary: Immunefi bounty of $1,000,000. Frontier's transfer truncated msg.value from 256 to 128 bits, so contracts could accept a large value that was actually truncated, enabling minting of unbacked wrapped assets across the three chains.

title: Tranchess ShareStaking skipped _checkpoint() allows draining staker funds around a rebalance
summary: Maximum $200,000 bounty. ShareStaking.deposit() derives spareAmount from the fund's tranche balance minus the tracked total supply, but _checkpoint() is skipped when already called in the same block; by checkpointing before a rebalance an attacker makes the stale supply drainable. Reported impact: up to ~815.1 BTC and ~1,438.5 ETH at risk on BSC; mitigated in 18h, permanent fix 6 days later, no losses.

title: Fuel Sway ABI type confusion lets a bool argument arrive as a non-boolean value
summary: Immunefi Attackathon writeup. Sway ABI argument handling validates the type but not the content of compound types, so a bool parameter can be delivered as a value other than 0 or 1; the writeup builds a PoC around this undefined-behaviour boolean and discusses how it can be weaponised across contract calls in FuelVM.

title: Angle Protocol: direct theft of user funds via AngleRouter::mixer reentrancy
summary: Critical Immunefi submission (marked not paid in the Immunefi writeup index). BaseRouter::mixer has no reentrancy guard; with an ERC777 token an attacker re-enters during a batched transfer or swap and sweeps the router's balance up to the victim's slippage, and unswept leftovers are callable by anyone.

title: Angle Protocol: theft of user funds by creating a vault in the middle of a batched router call
summary: Critical Immunefi submission (marked not paid). VaultManager::createVault is not nonReentrant and can be re-entered through onERC721Received; an attacker who creates vaultID 0 mid-batch in a victim's Router::mixerVaultManagerPermit call captures the victim's subsequent addCollateral and borrow operations.

title: Hourglass (old CLOB): order overwrite in OrderBook mapping keys blocks users permanently
summary: Critical report against the earlier Hourglass CLOB (explicitly not the current Hourglass Immunefi program). Orders are keyed only by (chain_id, sell_token, buy_token), so anyone can place a tiny order on the same pair, overwrite the victim's Pair state and call send() to set isAwaiting, permanently blocking the victim's order.

title: WardenSwap router permanently locks ETH sent alongside an ERC20 swap
summary: Low-severity report, $1k bounty. WardenRouterV2.swap() accepts msg.value together with valid ERC20 parameters but neither uses nor refunds the ETH, locking it permanently in a contract that cannot receive native ETH.

title: UniLend interest-rate miscalculation from missing 1e18 scaling of the base rate

title: Mimir Markets: private VS claim bearer key exposed in calldata

A private VS claim's bearer invite key was visible in creation, rematch and challenge calldata, so a stranger could join, occupy a slot and consume fixed liability or pool capacity; fix authorises msg.sender against creator-managed per-claim wallet grants. A second medium finding: paused undisputed proposals could neither finalize nor refund after the dispute window.

title: RadarDEX LaunchFactory pool-squat: attacker pre-creates the Uniswap pool at a fake price

LaunchFactory assumes Uniswap V3 createPool() always creates a fresh pool; an attacker can pre-create the pool at a fake price so the victim's launch adds its entire supply there and the attacker sells it, costing only gas. Lists core contract 0x6b3355aCd2F90BEEeEB7964AA1f83b3F866e53E9 on Arc (chainId 5042).

title: TollyPad createToken pool-initialization front-running (TOCTOU)

title: JustLend DAO liquidation front-running through the public TRON mempool

Source analysis only, no exploitation attempted.

title: Argus Launchpad graduate() never validates the created pool price
summary: Critical (CVSS 9.8), confirmed by decompiling the implementation. graduate() delegates pool creation to a portal contract but never checks the resulting pool price, enabling a pool-squat/front-run that captures the launch liquidity; report includes the decompiled selector 0xd3618cca and a proposed post-creation price check.

Timeline in the post records the bounty on 2023-04-14.

title: [Security Disclosure] DG weakness reported through Immunefi (funds not at risk)
summary: An anonymous whitehat reported a griefing vulnerability in Lido's Dual Governance RageQuit mechanism on 2025-07-13 via Immunefi. If triggered (requires >10% of stETH supply in the opposition escrow, a very unlikely state), it could significantly delay withdrawal of all ETH queued in an active RageQuit round. Lido assessed high potential impact and low likelihood, kept the Emergency Committee on standby, and targeted a fix for the August 2025 onchain vote; funds were not affected and the bug was not exploited.

title: Ahhhh i'm liquidating! - Deri Protocol force-liquidation writeup
summary: 0xriptide's writeup of a critical Deri bug: GatewayImplementation::finishLiquidate lacks the _checkRequestId nonce check used by finishRemoveMargin/finishUpdateLiquidity, and its ABI struct decodes the remove-margin uint256 requiredMargin as int256 cumulativePnlOnEngine. Anyone can replay a signed requestRemoveMargin eventData/signature into finishLiquidate, force-liquidate a healthy position, steal the trader's PnL and corrupt lastCumulativePnlOnEngine for all users; incorrect decimals widen the impact. Deri had ~$3m TVL across zkSync Era, Linea, Arbitrum, Polygon zkEVM and Scroll.

title: Vulnerability disclosure 2022-1-30 - SingleSidedBalancer strategy
summary: Whitehat report filed 2022-01-30 via Immunefi against Yearn's SingleSidedBalancer strategy: the design assigned withdrawal losses to the strategy instead of the withdrawing user, so an attacker could flashloan DAI/USDC, imbalance Balancer's 3pool, then withdraw the ~$41m of yvUSDT liquidity borrowed from Bentobox, forcing the strategy to buy USDT at an inflated price and leaving the loss to remaining depositors. Mitigated within 25 minutes of receipt; Yearn paid the maximum $200,000 bounty (USDC) on 2022-02-02.

title: Wormhole uninitialized implementation - $10M bounty
summary: Whitehat satya0x reported on 2022-02-24 that Wormhole's upgraded implementation contract had been left uninitialized, letting an attacker take control of the implementation behind the bridge proxy; Immunefi's published PoC notes $1.8 billion of assets were in the contract at submission and that the attacker could have held the protocol ransom by threatening to brick the Ethereum bridge. The bug was patched before exploitation and Wormhole paid $10 million, the largest bounty payout on record.

title: Security Disclosure - ICON Validators at Risk
summary: FuzzingLabs says it privately disclosed a serious vulnerability in the ICON node client via Immunefi that directly affects all validator nodes on the network. Per the thread, ICON leadership stayed silent with no fixes and no public communication, and the ICON Foundation cancelled its bug bounty program shortly after the report. No public technical writeup was located; the firm's blog host was unreachable at collection time.

title: Balancer MerkleOrchard responsible disclosure - 50 ETH bounty
summary: Balancer awarded a 50 ETH bounty to 0xriptide for a responsible disclosure made through Immunefi even though MerkleOrchard was not part of the Balancer bug bounty scope, citing the relevance of the report. The announcement gives no severity rating or technical detail, and no public report was linked.

title: THORChain critical submission dispute (~$270k)
summary: Luke Parker (kayabaNerve) says THORChain removed its Immunefi bug bounty program - which had received multiple critical-severity reports - in favour of a self-hosted process, and alleges this was part of ghosting his critical-severity submission after Immunefi ruled he should be paid roughly $270k. The report itself was never published and the dispute appears unresolved.

title: Private critical exploit chain in an unnamed Cosmos-based project (StateDB underflow)
summary: ControlZ says that about three weeks after reading KiiChain's postmortem they privately reported a critical exploit chain to another Cosmos-based project that reached the same unsafe StateDB native-balance subtraction (uint256 wrap-around) through a completely different path. The project confirmed and fixed it quickly. The post stresses the subtraction is only a primitive: exploitation still needs another accounting bug that breaks the balance check and a way to turn the broken balance into real money. The underlying report is unpublished.

title: Immunefi: $3,000,000 single critical smart-contract payout to ily2
summary: Immunefi announced that researcher ily2 earned $3,000,000 for a single critical smart contract bug - described as the largest single payout in web3 security in recent memory - across 3 submissions, all of which were paid. The program and the vulnerability are not named in the announcement.

title: Immunefi: $150,000 first paid report (critical blockchain/DLT)
summary: Immunefi announced that @ipwning earned a $150K bounty on a first paid report for a critical blockchain/DLT vulnerability, landing at #5 on the Immunefi 90-day leaderboard. The affected program and technical details are not disclosed in the post.

title: Immunefi: $50,000 critical blockchain/DLT payout to bpop23293
summary: Immunefi announced that researcher bpop23293 (@Ehsan1579) earned $50,000 for a critical blockchain/DLT disclosure. The same researcher later published the $200k zkSync Lite validity-rollup writeup (2026-01-20), but this post does not name the affected program.

title: PancakeSwap lottery contract whitehat disclosure and postmortem
summary: Immunefi says it facilitated a whitehat disclosure to patch a vulnerability in PancakeSwap's lottery contract, after which PancakeSwap launched a $1,000,000 bug bounty. Immunefi posted a postmortem of the lottery contract vulnerability and fix in the thread. The lead post gives no severity, and the technical detail sits in the follow-up thread post rather than the announcement.

title: Audit Competitions Beat Private Audits on Every Metric That Matters
summary: Immunefi CEO Mitchell Amador analysed all 1,178 public audit reports from Trail of Bits, Zellic and OpenZeppelin: the median report finds zero critical or high findings and the average is about 1.5 serious bugs per engagement, versus 6.2 per Immunefi audit competition. Cost per critical/high is roughly $66K in a T1 private audit against $6,548 in a competition. The piece is a quantitative baseline for how little of a private audit's findings surface publicly.

title: How Responsible are Spearbit and Cantina for Cork's $12M Hack?
summary: Long-form X article re-examining the 28 May 2025 Cork exploit ($12M, 3,761 wstETH). It contrasts the Sherlock, Quantstamp and Runtime Verification reports, which publish commit hashes and public repos, with Cantina's Dec 2024 private competition report, whose scope cannot be independently verified: the portfolio links cantina-forks/cork-monorepo, which now returns 404 (private), and the PDF has no scope/commit section. It also asks why a May 2025 Spearbit audit, reportedly paid through Uniswap's V4 hooks grant (15-business-day publication rule), was not released. Cork's own postmortem lists a May 2025 full-protocol audit as 'not yet published' and states that none of its audits flagged the Cork Hook access-control flaw.

title: cork-protocol - Cantina Private Competition report
summary: 17-page Cantina private-competition report (engagement 18 Dec 2024 - 9 Jan 2025, report dated 11 Mar 2025) for cork-protocol: 11 issues - 4 high, 2 medium, 2 low, 3 informational; all 4 high and both medium are marked fixed. The high findings are MEV/slippage issues in ERC-2612 swaps, reserve sales and redeemEarlyLv. The PDF is public and its PoCs reference CorkHook, indicating the hook was in scope; the portfolio page carries commit 51bb275bd583c75cdf5496cebfb87144035cdf75 but the linked repo is private (404), so the exact audited scope remains unverifiable. This report is not in the collected Cantina index.

title: 23,625 smart-contract vulnerabilities dataset sourced from private audit reports
summary: Researcher Zaevlad released a 23,625-finding dataset assembled over a year from private audit reports and contest platforms; each entry has title, description, PoC code, recommendation and severity. Published as a Hugging Face dataset (503 downloads, 109 likes at check) and the LazyAuditor GitHub repo (28 stars, created 2026-08-31). The author says the data is raw and needs deduplication and severity/label normalisation before ML training.

title: 5 Private Audit Market Trends Q2 2026
summary: Cyfrin's Dacian lists five Q2 2026 private-audit trends. Most relevant to this layer: more protocols keep audit reports private and deploy unverified contracts as 'security by obscurity', which he warns fails against closed MEV contracts being exploited and improving AI-assisted decompilation. Other trends: larger AI-generated codebases, fewer follow-up manual audits in favour of AI scans, pre-audit AI scans, and security-researcher redundancies.

title: Are acknowledged critical/high private audit findings legit? (poll)
summary: Poll of 179 voters: 69.8% say a critical/high private-audit finding is inflated if the protocol merely acknowledges it, 30.2% accept it. Replies discuss acknowledged-but-unfixed findings, including a claimed case where a protocol acknowledged a critical with a PoC. Useful as evidence that private findings can be acknowledged without being remediated or disclosed.

title: The Death of the Audit Contest? A 2025 Retrospective
summary: Researcher alix40 argues audit-contest platforms pivoted to private audits because margins are healthier, top security researchers followed the private work, and public contests are now flooded with low-quality and AI-generated submissions. Conditional pots and platform fees falling to 10-20% broke the incentive alignment between researchers, protocols and platforms.

title: Day 6-16 of trying to land a private audit
summary: Running thread by a researcher trying to break into private audits. Day 6 covers bug-bounty work on the STBL contracts (informational, out-of-scope and duplicate findings) and lessons on validating findings with a 'lawyer mindset'; adjacent posts cover DodoLimit and Nado (day 5), studying five prior audit reports for Inverse Finance's bounty programme (day 15), and networking with experienced auditors (day 16). No specific vulnerability details are disclosed.

title: Redacted (CosmWasm) private audit concluded
summary: ret2basic announced completion of a CosmWasm private audit for Redacted with getfailsafe, his first CosmWasm engagement, and said a series of CosmWasm audit reports would be released soon. No findings, severity or report link were disclosed.

title: First private audit to 10 engagements in three months
summary: Researcher BengalCatBalu recounts joining a first private audit in Dec 2025 and reaching 10 private engagements by Feb 2026, alongside publishing the EIP Security Handbook. No protocol names, findings or report links.

title: HackenProof hybrid model: audit contest plus solo private audit
summary: HackenProof announced a hybrid engagement for Dexlyn Labs: a $15,000 crowdsourced contest running in parallel with a hand-picked solo auditor paid separately for a private audit. The solo-track details were still to be announced.

title: Zaros private audit (Cyfrin) preceding the $60K contest
summary: Dacian, lead auditor of Cyfrin's private audit of Zaros, notes the code changed significantly during mitigation review and two features (signed off-chain orders and referrals) were added before the CodeHawks contest, raising the chance of contest findings. No private findings are disclosed.

title: Unpublished audit thread (content protected)
summary: Search snippet reads '4) Unpublished audit. "Pashov audit in progress..."', suggesting a list of unpublished/private audit items, but the account limits post visibility. Only the search snippet was visible; no content could be verified.

title: The Balancer Exploit: How Olympix Would Have Prevented the $121M Loss
summary: Post-incident analysis of the Nov 3, 2025 Balancer V2 drain (~$121.1M across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Polygon and Sonic). Asymmetric rounding in Composable Stable Pools (mulDown on upscale vs divUp/divDown on downscale) let crafted EXACT_OUT micro-swaps inside batchSwap underpay and quietly erode the invariant D. About $45.7M was protected or recovered, including $19.3M via pool pauses and $21.8M by a StakeWise DAO emergency operation.

title: GMX's $40M Exploit and How Olympix Would Have Prevented It
summary: Analysis of the July 9, 2025 GMX V1 exploit on Arbitrum. A user-controlled receiver in decreasePosition reentered Vault.increasePosition, bypassing PositionRouter/PositionManager, skewing the BTC short average price and inflating GLP; the attacker redeemed GLP at the inflated price for over $40M. GMX fell ~28% and trading was halted on Arbitrum and Avalanche.

title: The Truebit Exploit: How Olympix Would Have Prevented the $26.6M Loss
summary: Analysis of the first major 2026 DeFi exploit: ~8,535 ETH (~$26.6M) drained from Truebit's 2021 Purchase contract. An integer overflow in Solidity 0.6.10 bonding-curve code that had never had a public third-party audit let the attacker mint TRU for free; a second attacker took ~$224K and TRU fell ~99.9%.

title: SwapNet's $13.4M Loss and How Olympix Would Have Prevented It
summary: Summary of Matcha's post-mortem for the Jan 25, 2026 SwapNet exploit. The router made an arbitrary external call with a caller-supplied target and calldata, so a swap request could be turned into transferFrom against standing token approvals. $13.43M was taken from 18 users across Base, BNB Chain and Arbitrum ($13.34M from a single wallet) before the contracts were paused.

title: The YieldBlox Exploit: How Olympix Would Have Prevented the $10M Loss
summary: Analysis of the Feb 22, 2026 YieldBlox DAO exploit on Stellar. The pool operator configured a VWAP oracle against a near-zero-liquidity market with no circuit breakers or sanity checks, allowing price manipulation; ~$10.2M was lost, of which ~$7.2M was frozen by Stellar Tier-1 validators and ~$3M remained unrecovered.

title: Resupply Exploit Post-Mortem: How Olympix Would Have Prevented the $9.56M Loss
summary: Post-mortem of the June 26, 2025 Resupply exploit. A donation attack on a newly deployed, empty ERC-4626 cvcrvUSD vault inflated its exchange rate; $9.56M was drained in about 90 minutes and the protocol set borrow limits to zero an hour later.

title: Bonzo Lend's $9.05M Loss and How Olympix Would Have Prevented It
summary: Analysis citing Bonzo's own incident report for the July 11, 2026 exploit on Hedera. Supra's on-chain oracle verifier accepted a [0,0] BLS signature against an unset committee key, so a forged SAUCE price ~12 orders of magnitude too high let the attacker borrow 6.63M USDC and 34.52M WHBAR against 250 SAUCE and leave ~$9.05M in bad debt.

title: Moonwell's $8.7M Loss and How Olympix Would Have Prevented It
summary: Analysis of the Aug 27, 2026 Moonwell incident on Base. 53.4M MAMO were transferred straight to the mMAMO market contract instead of being deposited, bypassing a supply cap that only counted deposits; the inflated collateral exchange rate let the attacker borrow ~$11.03M of cbBTC, WETH, USDC and wstETH, bridge ~$8.7M out and leave ~$9.13M of borrower obligations (Moonwell post-mortem dated Aug 28).

title: Verus Ethereum Bridge's $7.5M Loss and How Olympix Would Have Prevented It
summary: Analysis of the July 23, 2026 Verus-Ethereum bridge drain. submitImports checked a transfer list against its hash but never against the value locked on the Verus side, so a 0.01 VRSC export authorized a payout of 1,137.45 ETH, 71.5 tBTC, stablecoins, MKR and 220,357 freshly minted DAI (~$7.54M) to one wallet.

title: JaredFromSubway's $7.5M Loss and How Olympix Would Have Prevented It
summary: Analysis of the June 20, 2026 theft from the jaredfromsubway.eth sandwich bot. An attacker built a fake market the bot would target, let it win small amounts for about 21 hours, then used the bot's leftover token approvals to take ~$7.5M in WETH, USDC and USDT in a single transaction at 18:49:11 UTC.

title: Summer.fi's $6M Loss and How Olympix Would Have Prevented It
summary: Analysis of the July 6, 2026 Summer.fi exploit. Vault share price was the sum of strategy balances anyone could donate to; the attacker bought ~$40K of impaired Silo Varlamore USDC shares, donated them to a strategy still valued near par, flash-borrowed $65.4M USDC and redeemed for ~$6.04M (about $5.64M from the Lower Risk USDC vault).

title: X100's $4.75M Loss and How Olympix Would Have Prevented It
summary: Analysis of the Oct 24, 2026 X100 governance exploit. A single flash-funded transaction bought two of the three Senate seats, and the passed proposal (described on-chain as 'testnet flash governance proof') made the treasury sell 400,000 X for 35.675313 USDT; the attacker left with 4,749,726 USDT. Blockaid traced roughly $4.85M across all exploit transactions.

title: New Market Trading's $4M Loss and How Olympix Would Have Prevented It
summary: Analysis of the May 25, 2026 New Market Trading exploit. The SquidRouterModule Safe module's cross-chain entry point lacked a caller check and took the delegate address from the attacker's message, so 88 client Safes were swapped into a worthless token; ~$3.98M was drained across Ethereum, Base and Arbitrum.

title: Nostra Finance's $3.5M Loss and How Olympix Would Have Prevented It
summary: Analysis of the Sept 17, 2026 Nostra Finance exploit on Starknet. The Pragma oracle averaged a thin attacker-made NSTR pool (price ~$99) with the real price, so about $421 of NSTR collateral supported ~$3.5M of borrowing.

title: The $2.7M Solv Protocol Exploit and How Olympix Would Have Prevented It
summary: Analysis of the March 5, 2026 Solv Protocol exploit. onERC721Received and onERC3525Received lacked nonReentrant, enabling cross-function reentrancy through mint(); the attacker turned 135 BRO into ~567M and drained 38.05 SolvBTC (~$2.7M) over 22 repetitions.

title: Post-Mortem: Hyperbridge MMR Verifier Exploit, April 13, 2026
summary: Project post-mortem published May 14, 2026. Leaves whose index fell outside every peak were silently left over in the MMR verifier's iterator, so a proof containing one forged leaf reconstructed a genuine root and passed verification, draining the Token Gateway (~$2.5M realized). The fix adds an OutOfBoundsLeaves invariant; the incident triggered an SRLabs audit (14 findings: 1 critical, 3 high) and private disclosures to the Polkadot SDK and rs-merkle maintainers.

title: Smart Contract Incident Report: Legacy Bridge Vulnerability
summary: thirdweb incident report dated Dec 12, 2025. A legacy Bridge contract (0x81d57DD01a15BC1C19563693902df621500D4d2A) was never decommissioned during the April 10, 2025 front-running fix, so an attacker could still spend users' unlimited ERC20 approvals. Impact was limited to a single wallet on Ethereum mainnet, native balances were unaffected, and the proxy was upgraded to a null implementation on Dec 11; thirdweb says it did not publish the loss amount.

title: Bond Protocol Incident Report
summary: Incident report published Oct 24, 2022 on the Oct 21, 2022 Fixed-Expiry Teller exploit. redeem() did not validate the bond token, so a counterfeit ERC20 bond token with OHM as the underlying drained 30,437 vesting OHM (~$300K) from three OlympusDAO markets. The individual returned all funds to OlympusDAO the same day and the Teller was replaced.

title: Critical Bug Identified in 88mph Awarded with $42,069 Bounty
summary: iosiro write-up published June 15, 2021 on a critical re-initialization bug found June 7, 2021 and reported through Immunefi for a $42,069 bounty. The NFT contract's initializer lacked a one-time check, letting anyone take ownership, burn and re-mint deposit NFTs and withdraw the underlying assets, then worth over $6.5M across three pools. 88mph restricted the function within 2 hours and moved funds to the treasury within 24 hours; no funds were lost.

title: Drift Protocol Incident: Multisig Governance Compromise via Durable Nonce Exploitation
summary: BlockSec/Phalcon analysis published April 3, 2026, while Drift had released only an initial statement and no full post-mortem. Attackers induced two of five Security Council signers to pre-sign governance transactions held in durable nonce accounts (surviving a March 27 multisig migration), executed an admin takeover with zero timelock, listed a worthless CVT market with an attacker-controlled oracle, and drained $285,279,417.69 in 31 withdrawals over about 12 minutes.

title: V12 Says THORChain Silently Patched Its Critical Bug, Then Told Researchers the Bounty Is 'Permanently Retired'
summary: The Defiant report published June 1, 2026 on V12's disclosure dispute. V12 says it reported a critical proposer-forgery bug on April 28, 2026 and was told the bounty program was permanently retired; THORChain says the program closed before the submission and that the reported bug is unrelated to the May 15, 2026 $10.7M Asgard vault exploit, which Blockaid and ZachXBT attributed to a near-identical proposer-forgery flaw. A May 6 fix commit failed CI and was never deployed, and THORChain has published no post-mortem.

title: Attacker can add arbitrary data to the blockchain without paying gas
summary: Missing end-of-input check in RSKj's Transaction::rlpParse lets an attacker append arbitrary RLP-encoded bytes to a valid transaction. The trailing data passes validation, propagates over the network and is accepted in a block, so arbitrary data reaches the RSK chain without paying gas. HackerOne critical (9.3), 258 upvotes.

title: Crafted smart contract can take 8 minutes to execute due to bug in modexp precompile.
summary: A bug in RSKj's modexp precompile lets a crafted smart contract stall execution for about eight minutes in the reporter's FINGERROOT reproducer. High (8.3); one of three gas-metering/DoS reports filed against the RSK EVM in June 2025.

title: Crafted smart contract can take 1.5 minutes to execute due to inefficient CODESIZE implementation
summary: VM.doCODESIZE() calls Program.getCode() and copies the entire contract byte array on every CODESIZE, so a crafted contract can move over 1 TB in aggregate and take about 1.5 minutes to execute. Medium; same RSKj gas-metering cluster as the modexp and error-string reports.

title: Crafted smart contract can take ~23 seconds to execute due to immense error string construction
summary: NativeContract.execute hex-encodes the entire invalid input into an error string; a 1,081,344-byte input inside an infinite loop costs about 23 seconds (70 s on the reporter's machine), making execution-time griefing cheap. Medium (6.1).

title: DoS through PeerExplorer
summary: Improper connection management in RSKj's PeerExplorer/NodeChallengeManager lets an attacker exhaust the established-connection table through the ping-pong handshake, denying peer discovery. High (7.7), $4,000.

title: DOS of RSKJ server
summary: A malformed UDP packet to RSKj's discovery port 5050 makes RLP.bytesToLength return -5 (length 0); the UDP server then processes only that packet and stops answering other nodes until the process crashes. High, $5,000.

title: Traffic amplification attack via discovery protocol
summary: RSKj's UDP discovery ping-pong accepts a pong whose source IP differs from the ping target, so an attacker can add a spoofed victim address to establishedConnections and send FindNodePeerMessage to make the node amplify traffic at a third party. Medium (4.9), $2,000.

title: JSON RPC methods for debugging enabled by default allow DoS
summary: Debug JSON-RPC methods were enabled by default on RSKj's public bounty node; a single evm_reset call hung the RPC server and left it synced at block 0. Medium (5.9).

title: Groups module can halt chain when handling a proposal with malicious group weights
summary: After the GHSA-x5vx-95h7-rv4p fix for a zero-total-power divide-by-zero in x/group, a proposal with malicious group weights still makes the decision-policy decimal division fail with an out-of-range exponent, which can halt the chain. High, $15,000.

title: Unauthorized coins transfer from locking account(s)
summary: MsgExecute packs a lockup SendCoins message whose msg.Sender is attacker-controlled; checkSender compares it with the account owner but nothing validates the outer sender, so anyone can move unlocked funds out of periodic-locking accounts they do not own. Critical.

title: Race condition in faucet when using starport
summary: A race condition in Starport's faucet lets one account bypass coins_max and claim more tokens than the configured limit. Critical (9.3), $5,000; first sent by email, then copied to HackerOne.

title: Attacker can use any non-enabled capability
summary: CosmWasm capabilities are enforced only through a contract-supplied required-capabilities string; a contract that omits it can call any chain action even when the chain advertises no such capability. Rated low but paid $2,000; privilege escalation across the wasm boundary.

title: ETH contract handling errors
summary: Business-logic error in Coinbase's ETH contract handling: a nested call that reverted could still credit a deposit even though funds had not been transferred, and delegatecall was mishandled. Critical (9.3); sample InternalAttacker contract in the report.

title: Ethereum account balance manipulation
summary: Coinbase credited ETH received from a contract even when the underlying contract execution failed, allowing account balance manipulation. Critical; Coinbase says it changed the contract-handling logic within hours and saw no exploitation attempts.

title: Authorization Bypass in Starknet Snap via enableAuthorize parameter leads to unauthorized transaction signing
summary: The Starknet Snap honors a website-controlled enableAuthorize=false and skips the confirmation dialog, so a malicious site can sign messages or transactions without user approval. HackerOne rated medium; paid $350.

title: Bypass parsing of transaction data, users on the phishing site will transfer/approve ERC20 tokens without being alerted
summary: MetaMask mis-parsed truncated calldata for ERC20 contracts compiled with solc <0.5.0 (which zero-pad short input), so a phishing site could make the wallet display one amount while the user transferred or approved another. Low (3.3), $1,000.

title: Missing Line Terminator on allowedOrigins enables origin spoofing
summary: A missing regex terminator in Snaps' allowedOrigins check let a malicious origin pass the allow-list and reach restricted Snaps APIs, including the Keyring API's exportAccount method. High (7.7); fixed before production.

title: total Failure of password protection while extracting seed phrase! increases attack surface area for scammers
summary: MetaMask extension UI code could read the seed phrase without password confirmation, violating the UI/background boundary; not directly exploitable but a serious hardening gap. Medium (6.1), $3,500, fixed in extension 11.7.1.

title: MetaMask Browser URL and Transaction Origin Spoofing - Metamask wallet Android & Metamask wallet iOS
summary: MetaMask Mobile's in-app browser did not update the tab's domain after a redirect, so transactions requested by a malicious dApp appeared to originate from the previously trusted site. High (7.1).

title: Zero-amount miner TX + RingCT allows monero wallet to receive arbitrary amount of monero
summary: A crafted miner transaction that still passes daemon verification makes a CLI wallet believe it received an attacker-chosen amount of XMR, which the reporter believed could be used to steal from exchanges. Critical; submitted by the lead developer of CUT coin.

title: A bug in the Monero wallet balance can enable theft from exchanges
summary: A wallet balance bug fixed by PR #3985 also affected exchanges: a 1 XMR transfer with a duplicated TX pub key is credited as 2 XMR, letting an attacker withdraw more than deposited and repeat. Critical; the reporter says it was already exploited on a Monero-derived coin.

title: Constant-time comparison is not always implemented; critical areas are vulnerable to key-timing attacks
summary: Constant-time comparison is not implemented across RingCT key containers and rctOps equalKeys, leaving key comparisons vulnerable to timing attacks. Critical; the reporter could not assess exploit difficulty.

title: Critical Deadlock Vulnerability in Monero RPC Leading to Complete Node Paralysis
summary: A single unauthenticated JSON-RPC batch request deadlocks monerod permanently (CVSS 10.0), affecting v0.18.4.2 and likely all earlier versions, all operating systems and restricted-RPC mode. Critical.

title: Authenticated `unsigned_txset` change spoof lets a malicious hot wallet steal cold-signer change
summary: A malicious hot/watch-only wallet holding the victim's view key can forge an authenticated unsigned_txset so the cold signer presents an attacker-spendable output as change and signs it; direct loss of funds in monero-wallet-cli cold signing. High.

title: Loss of multisig funds through single malicious participant's deliberate deception
summary: A malicious multisig participant can claim a signing round failed, have co-signers sign a second transaction from a different input to the same recipient, then broadcast both, double-paying and draining the multisig. Medium.

title: `check_reserve_proof` sums RingCT ECDH amounts without checking the output commitment
summary: check_reserve_proof decodes RingCT ECDH amounts and sums them without recomputing the Pedersen commitment and comparing it to outPk[n].mask, so a malicious prover can present an amount not bound to the output commitment and overstate the proven reserve. Medium (4.7).

title: SpendProofV1 txid-substitution: get_spend_proof/check_spend_proof do not verify returned transaction hash
summary: get_spend_proof/check_spend_proof build the challenge from the caller-supplied txid instead of the hash of the returned transaction blob and never compare tx_hash to txid, enabling txid substitution. Medium (5.3).

title: It's possible to put SDX orderbook into invalid state and execute trades at arbitrary price
summary: stellar-core mishandles a buy offer that crosses existing sells but is only partially fillable because of a trustline limit, leaving the SDEX orderbook invalid and allowing trades at arbitrary prices. High (8.2).

title: Exploitable vulnerability in SDEX
summary: SDEX executes minimum-size (0.0000001) trades at 1:1 regardless of the price set in MANAGE_ORDER because of rounding, letting an attacker buy BTC for 0.0000001 XLM and repeat. High (7.2).

title: Reentrancy attack in eth-monero atomic swap
summary: A reentrancy in noot's eth-xmr atomic swap contract lets an attacker drain almost all ETH (all but 1 ETH); the reporter notes it is published reference code not known to be deployed and rated it low. HackerOne severity was left unset.

title: DOS attack by consuming all CPU and using all available memory
summary: Listed in the reddelexc/hackerone-reports dataset as a $1,500 Tron Foundation bounty, but the HackerOne report JSON returned HTTP 404 on 2026-11-08, so no primary content could be read. Title and bounty are from the dataset only; severity and date are unavailable.

title: Private key "tron" leaked via Travis CI Log
summary: Listed in the reddelexc/hackerone-reports dataset as a $1,000 Tron Foundation bounty for a private key exposed in a Travis CI log, but the HackerOne report JSON returned HTTP 404 on 2026-11-08. Title and bounty are from the dataset only; severity and date are unavailable.

title: Discord Link expired - Possible vanity address could be used to link a malicious Discord server.
summary: An expired Discord invite on Zilliqa's vanity URL was repointed to an attacker-controlled Discord server, letting a malicious user phish Zilliqa users. P3, 10 points, resolved; the only blockchain-program disclosure found in Bugcrowd's public crowdstream.

title: Vyper, Curve Exploit Post-Mortem
summary: Metronome's msETH-ETH Curve pool was drained on 2023-07-30 in the wider Vyper compiler exploit affecting pools deployed with v0.2.15, v0.2.16 or v0.3.0 that held naked ETH. MEV bots front-ran the attacker; c0ffeebabe returned 786.5 ETH and 955 msETH, Metronome recovered another 157,500 USDC, and the team seeded a new msETH-WETH pool for affected LPs.

title: 10/18/24 Incident Post Mortem
summary: On 2024-10-18 a North Korean 'contagious interview' attack compromised a core contributor's private keys, letting the attacker mint 315.5 trillion USDO and steal 29.6M TAP to drain the USDO/USDC and TAP/ETH pools for about $4.65M (605 ETH plus 3.1M USDC). The post documents the single-signer hot-wallet admin setup, the on-chain tracing, and the recovery status.

title: Cauldron V4 Post Mortem
summary: A re-entrancy in CauldronV4's init() let an attacker deploy a clone with a malicious Oracle and re-enter the cook() call action before the blacklisting step, exposing tokens that 44 users had approved to DegenBox across the GLP, CRV, migrated WBTC and yvcrvstETH cauldrons. No user or protocol funds were lost; the team executed a whitehat rescue and opened a claims contract.

title: An attack on V3Utils
summary: On 2023-02-18 just under $30K was stolen from users of Revert's 'Atomic swaps into V3 positions' feature through the V3Utils contract. The team disabled the feature, reconstructed the approval-abuse path, and reimbursed every affected user by airdrop on Mainnet, Optimism, Polygon and Arbitrum.

title: zkLink Nova Exploit Post-Mortem
summary: On 2026-10-28 a single Ethereum transaction drained both zkLink Nova escrows for about $743k (22.43 ETH plus 11 ERC-20 tokens, led by 245.74 pufETH). The root cause was Arbitrator.claimMessage() making an arbitrary external call with the Arbitrator's trusted identity, combined with an EIP-1153 transient-storage latch that was never cleared, so a forged Merkle root could be written and withdrawn against. A copycat drained four more chains nine hours later, and the system was still unpatched at the time of writing.

title: Permanent Chain Split in Movement Full Node: Anatomy of a $6,710 Critical Vulnerability That Required a Hard Fork
summary: Yunus Emre Sarıtoprak describes a missing fork-choice check in process_block_from_da() in execute_settle.rs that allowed two blocks at the same height, risking a permanent chain split and double-spends. The issue was responsibly disclosed through Immunefi, fixed by a mandatory hard fork, and paid a $6,710 bounty.

title: Sky Remote Code Execution Bugfix Review
summary: Researcher xss found that vote.makerdao.com passed user-supplied Markdown to the gray-matter library with its JavaScript engine enabled, so a malicious .md URL in a poll could execute system commands and read files such as /etc/passwd. The issue was fixed on 2023-09-28 and paid the maximum critical bounty of $50,000.

title: Aztec Multiple-Spend Error Bugfix Review
summary: LonelySloth disclosed a multiple-spend error in Aztec's codebase on 2023-09-12 that could have drained the entire roughly $5M TVL. Aztec mitigated the issue quickly and paid a $450,000 bounty.

title: Alchemix Missing Solvency Check Bugfix Review
summary: KoiushSec reported on 2023-09-28 that missing solvency checks at liquidation would let an attacker with significant upfront capital mint over 7,000 unbacked alETH in two hours, then worth about $11.66M. Alchemix fixed the issue with no loss and paid 9,100 ACLX, about $116,513.

title: Inside the Kelp/LayerZero Hack: How Lazarus Forged $292M Into Existence
summary: On 2026-04-18 Kelp's Ethereum bridge released $292M after a forged LayerZero verification path that Lazarus Group manipulated through trusted verifier infrastructure. The attacker used the stolen rsETH as Aave collateral, leaving roughly $200M of bad debt and locking WETH suppliers out of their funds; the post reconstructs the six-layer forgery and the cross-protocol cascade.

title: The Silent Yield Killer: How Unscaled Integer Division Trapped Farming Rewards in a Top DEX

# Cross-chain TempleGold transfers do not work for users with account abstraction wallets

### Severity
Low Risk

## Summary

TempleGold token cross-chain transfers only allow transferring them to the same address on various chains. 

`if (msg.sender != _to) { revert ITempleGold.NonTransferrable(msg.sender, _to); }`

Since account abstraction wallets do not have the same address on different chains, they are disallowed from using this feature - which is possibly an unexpected bug.

## Vulnerability Details

As written in summary, the vulnerability stems from the fact TempleGold tokens can not be cross-chained by users who use account abstraction. Account abstraction wallets do not necessarily have the same address on different chains.

## Impact

Big part of the community and users are cut off from the protocol.

## Tools Used

Manual review

## Recommendations

We detect that the only reason for this limitation is for users to not be able to transfer TempleGold tokens between various wallets. But as described in impact - it introduces limitations for a GREAT number of users.

Introduce mechanism for account abstraction wallets to be able to correctly bridge TempleGold tokens on different chains.

High Risk

## Summary

In the `MembershipFactory`, a vulnerability was identified in the mechanism used for managing upgradeable proxies through the `ProxyAdmin` pattern. The issue arises from improper chaining of `ProxyAdmin` contracts, which effectively disables the intended upgrade functionality of the `TransparentUpgradeableProxy`. This malfunction  will prevent the future upgrading of proxy contracts.

## Vulnerability Details

The flawed logic in the proxy administration setup stems from the following sequence of actions within the `MembershipFactory` contract:

1. **ProxyAdmin Initialization:** The `MembershipFactory` constructor creates an initial `ProxyAdmin` contract (`proxyAdminA`) with `msg.sender` as the owner. This setup is supposed to facilitate control over proxy contracts for upgrades.

   ```Solidity
   proxyAdmin = new ProxyAdmin(msg.sender);
   ```

2. **Creation of TransparentUpgradeableProxy:** When deploying a new `TransparentUpgradeableProxy`, `proxyAdminA` is used as the `initialOwner` input parameter:

   ```Solidity
   TransparentUpgradeableProxy proxy = new TransparentUpgradeableProxy(
       membershipImplementation,
       address(proxyAdmin), 
       abi.encodeWithSignature("initialize(string,string,string,address,address)", daoConfig.ensname, "OWP", baseURI, _msgSender(), daoConfig.currency)
   ```

# Lack of Access Control Allows Unauthorized DAO Creation and Entry Without KYC Verification

### Severity
Low Risk

## Summary

The functions `createNewDAOMembership` and `joinDAO` are publicly accessible, allowing any address to create or join a DAO without restriction. Although the platform's website indicates that users must undergo a KYC/AML (Know Your Customer) process before creating or joining DAOs, there is currently no mechanism enforcing this requirement on-chain. As a result, users can bypass KYC verification and interact directly with these functions, undermining the intended security checks.

## Impact

This vulnerability allows unauthorized users to bypass KYC requirements and interact with the DAO creation and entry functions, which could result in:

* Regulatory compliance risks by permitting unverified users to access sensitive areas of the protocol.
* Potential for abuse if unverified users create/Join DAOs for malicious or unintended purposes.

POC

```Solidity
it("unauthorizedDao could be created", async function () {
      await currencyManager.addCurrency(await testERC20.getAddress());  // Assume addCurrency function exists in CurrencyManager
      const [unauthorizedUser] = await ethers.getSigners();
      await membershipFactory.connect(unauthorizedUser).createNewDAOMembership(DAOConfig, TierConfig);      
      const ensToAddress = await membershipFactory.getENSAddress("unauthorizedDao.eth");
      
      expect(await membershipFactory.userCreatedDAOs(unauthorizedUser, "unauthorizedDao.eth")).to.equal(ensToAddress);
});

CONSOLE:
\Audits\hh> npx hardhat test --grep "unauthorizedDao should not be created"


  MembershipFactory
    POC MembershipFactory
      ✔ unauthorizedDao could be created


  1 passing (1s)
```

## Tools Used

* Manual
* Hardhat

## Recommendations

1. **Require OWPIdentity NFT Ownership**: Enforce that users hold an `OWPIdentity` NFT from the protocol to validate they have passed KYC before they can call `createNewDAOMembership` or `joinDAO`. This would ensure only verified users can interact with these functions.
2. **Signature-Based Access Control**: Alternatively, implement a permissions system based on signed messages, where only users with a valid KYC signature from an authorized party can access these functions. This would reduce the reliance on NFTs and allow for flexible KYC verification.

```solidity
// settlementFee = liquidationFee

    feeRecipients: FeeRecipients.Data({
        marginCollateralRecipient: globalConfiguration.marginCollateralRecipient,
        orderFeeRecipient: address(0),
        settlementFeeRecipient: globalConfiguration.liquidationFeeRecipient
    }),
>>  pnlUsdX18: requiredMaintenanceMarginUsdX18, // @audit-info Incorrect parameter
    orderFeeUsdX18: UD60x18_ZERO,
```

```solidity
>>  /// @param pnlUsdX18 The total unrealized PnL of the account.
```

# Liqudation fee is not take in cosideration during liqudation

### Severity
Medium Risk

## Summary

The protocol currently does not account for the liquidation fee when determining if a trading account is liquidatable. It is stated in the official documentation that this fee should be accounted during the check does a position is liquidatable.

## Vulnerability Details

When checking if a trading account should be liquidated, the protocol doesn't take in consideration the liquidation fee. This oversight can lead to scenarios where an account is considered non-liquidatable, even though, after accounting for the liquidation fee, it should be liquidated.

## Impact

If the margin goes below the required threshold without considering the liquidation fee, the fee may not be covered during liquidation. This could result in the protocol failing to collect the necessary fees.

## Tools Used

Manual review

## Recommendations

To fix this issue, update the isLiquidatable function to include the liquidation fee in its calculations:

```diff
function isLiquidatable(
        UD60x18 requiredMaintenanceMarginUsdX18,
        SD59x18 marginBalanceUsdX18
    )
        internal
        pure
        returns (bool)
    {
+       GlobalConfiguration.Data storage globalConfiguration = GlobalConfiguration.load();
+       return requiredMaintenanceMarginUsdX18.intoSD59x18().add(globalConfiguration.liquidationFeeUsdX18).gt(marginBalanceUsdX18);
-       return requiredMaintenanceMarginUsdX18.intoSD59x18().gt(marginBalanceUsdX18);
    }
```

This adjustment ensures that the liquidation process properly accounts for the liquidation fee, maintaining the protocol's financial integrity and preventing potential shortfalls.
